text:
Claire M: Following up on the RFC — I want to propose a concrete design for deferred-activation quantization + routing. TL;DR: keep weights quantized, but apply activation quantization only after a warmup window of N tokens to avoid early-token quality cliffs while still getting memory/throughput wins on long contexts.

Ben K: interesting. do you mean warmup per request or per session/kv-entry?

Claire M: per request. idea: for each generation request we start in "high-fidelity activation mode" for the first M tokens (prefill + immediate decode tokens), then switch activations to lower-bit path. This avoids early token hallucination spikes we saw in the FP8 experiments.

Alice Z: how do we detect M? static config vs adaptive?

Claire M: propose three knobs: 1) fixed warmup tokens (customer-configurable), 2) SNR-based auto-snap (runtime monitors per-token confidence and flips when stable), 3) profile-driven default (model-specific heuristic from evals).

Devon R: runtime implications: switching activation pipeline mid-request sounds tricky for kv cache and continuous-batching. will need to ensure cache format compatibility across modes.

Claire M: yes — big constraint. plan: keep a single KV representation (fp32 or quantized canonical) and perform mode switch at compute layer only. KV storage stays canonical to avoid format migration during request. switching means we route subsequent matmuls through quantized kernels and use quantized activation buffers.

Ben K: i worry about the extra memory of keeping canonical KV + activation buffers. does it eat all memory benefit?

Claire M: measured in microbenchmarks: for a 32k ctx GPT-style model, deferred activation quant gives ~28% peak memory reduction compared to always-fp32 activations, vs ~40% for always-quant activations. tradeoff seems decent, and avoids ~6-10% quality drop on early tokens we saw otherwise.

Alice Z: API surface? Is this something we expose to customers or keep as internal ops heuristic?

Claire M: propose a per-request fidelity dialect: e.g. 

```
"fidelity": {
  "activation_mode": "deferred|always|never",
  "warmup_tokens": 8,
  "fallback_threshold": 0.12  // per-token degscore threshold
}
```

Where activation_mode defaults to "deferred" for most open-model catalog entries, and customers can override. fallback_threshold ties into runtime quality monitor to force switch back to high-fidelity if degeneration is detected.

Devon R: nice and compact. ops concerns: need telemetry hooks for per-token degscore, mode switch timestamps, and memory/latency deltas so SRE can verify cost uplifts.

Frank O: ops-bot: canary window scheduled when Claire merges change. will trigger a canary on the 4-tiny test accounts. :white_check_mark:

Ben K: how about canary plan? progressive rollout?

Claire M: propose: stage 1 (internal bench) -> stage 2 (shadow traffic 0.1% with logging) -> stage 3 (canary 1% with automatic rollback if degscore regress > 1.5x baseline) -> stage 4 (gradual ramp). ops-bot will gate.

Devon R: compatibility note: quantized kernels must be idempotent on switch; we should add a kernel-level flag `activation_switch_id` so traces can correlate old/new path execution. also need a lint in codegen to prevent mixing mismatched residual scales across heads.

Alice Z: evaluation: propose to add an early-token focused eval set (20–50 token prompts) and a longctx eval set separately. measure BLEU/EM-like quality and also degscore + latency. include cost-per-request estimate.

Claire M: yes, plus run the "residual-scale preservation" tests — ensure quant path preserves norm of residuals within tolerance. if not, degrade to high-fidelity for that layer.

Ben K: thoughts on exposing to Dedicated/Private customers? they might want per-tenant defaults.

Claire M: make it tenant-configurable via the model manifest. default to our catalog heuristics but allow tenant override. for private installs we add a knob in the private config UI.

Devon R: one more runtime edge: prefill vs decode. If warmup includes only prefill tokens that are large batches, switching during decode (low throughput) may increase tail latency. we should allow `warmup_phase: prefill|decode|both` in the fidelity object.

Claire M: good call. update API sample accordingly.

Alice Z: can we prototype a simplified version that only supports static warmup_tokens and prefill-only switching? then iterate to adaptive SNR-based?

Claire M: exactly the plan. P0: static warmup_tokens + telemetry + canary. P1: adaptive SNR + per-layer fallbacks.

Frank O: ops-bot: canary created: canary-activation-quant-2026-03-24. will post metrics to #eng-sre.

Ben K: ok let's write the small RFC addendum (Claire/Devon) outlining runtime hook points (kv canonicalization, kernel switch id, trace markers) and Alice can add eval plan. I'll spin up an infra microbench to validate the memory numbers.

Claire M: thanks all — i'll draft the addendum and drop it here. :memo:
